title: NetworkManager and firewalld
subtitle: Configure the connection, verify DNS and routing, then open only the ports the service actually needs.
objectives: Read NetworkManager device and connection state
Configure IPv4 addressing and DNS with nmcli
Triage name resolution and route problems
Distinguish firewalld runtime from permanent configuration
Expose a service with a permanent firewall rule and verify it

ex200.evidence: nmcli device status and connection show.
nmcli connection modify for address, gateway, and DNS.
ip route, resolvectl or getent, and ping evidence.

versionNotes: NetworkManager and nmcli are the supported network configuration path on both RHEL 9 and RHEL 10. Do not hand-edit ifcfg files or assume network-scripts are available.
RHEL 10 uses the nftables backend for firewalld. The firewall-cmd interface is stable, but inspect the actual rules with nft when debugging rather than relying on old iptables habits.

sections.title: NetworkManager is the source of truth

commands.desc: Show interfaces, types, state, and active connections.
Inspect one profile’s addressing and DNS settings.

commands.cmd: sudo nmcli connection modify "Wired connection 1" ipv4.addresses 192.0.2.50/24
commands.desc: Set a static IPv4 address on a profile.
Read the routing table and interface addresses.
Open HTTP in the permanent firewall configuration.
Apply permanent firewall changes to runtime.
Show the active zone’s services and ports.

lab.title: A static profile and a deliberate opening
lab.scenario: Inspect the active connection, set a lab address and DNS server, verify name resolution, then open HTTP and 8443/tcp permanently and reload.

steps.text: Inspect device state and the active connection profile.
steps.cmd: nmcli device status && nmcli connection show
steps.verify: You can name the device and the saved connection profile.

steps.text: Set a static IPv4 address, gateway, and DNS server on the profile.
steps.cmd: sudo nmcli connection modify "Wired connection 1" ipv4.method manual ipv4.addresses 192.0.2.50/24 ipv4.gateway 192.0.2.1 ipv4.dns 192.0.2.53 && sudo nmcli connection up "Wired connection 1"
steps.verify: The profile reports manual IPv4 addressing and the intended DNS server.

steps.text: Verify DNS resolution and the route to the network.
steps.verify: Name resolution returns an address and a default route exists.

steps.text: Open HTTP and TCP 8443 permanently in the active zone.
steps.verify: The permanent configuration contains http and 8443/tcp.

steps.text: Reload firewalld and verify runtime state.
steps.verify: The active zone lists http and 8443/tcp after reload.

quiz.q: Which command shows NetworkManager device state and profile names?
quiz.why: nmcli device status lists the device, type, state, and active connection.

quiz.q: What is the difference between firewall-cmd runtime and permanent changes?
options: Runtime changes survive reboot; permanent changes do not
Permanent changes are saved but require reload or reboot to become runtime
quiz.why: The permanent configuration is on disk; --reload copies it into the active runtime rules.

quiz.q: Which tool tests name resolution through the system’s NSS configuration?
quiz.why: getent uses NSS and reflects how applications on this host resolve names.
